citeAs: Awadalla, A., Xue, L., Lo, O., Shu, M., Lee, H., Guha, E., Jordan, M., Shen, S., Awadalla, M., Savarese, S., Xiong, C., Xu, R., Choi, Y., Schmidt, L. (2024). MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv:2406.11271.
creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt (University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California Berkeley)
description: MINT-1T-PDF-CC-2024-18 is the PDF subset of MINT-1T sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files (February 2023 to April 2024 dumps), containing multimodal interleaved documents with sequences of images and text extracted from PDF files. It is part of MINT-1T, the largest open-source multimodal interleaved dataset with one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images total, including 93 billion tokens from the PDF subset.
name: MINT-1T-PDF-CC-2024-18
rai:dataBiases: The PDF subset has a higher proportion of Science and Technology documents compared to HTML sources, likely due to the nature of scientific communication where PDFs are the preferred format for sharing research papers and technical reports. The paper avoids model-based text quality heuristics (following RefinedWeb, Dolma, FineWeb practices) because such classifiers have been shown to favor text from certain demographics.
rai:dataCollection: PDF documents are sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files from February 2023 to April 2024 dumps. PDF links are extracted from these dumps, then downloaded and read using PyMuPDF. PDFs larger than 50MB or over 50 pages are discarded. Pages with no text are excluded. Reading order is obtained by finding bounding boxes of text blocks, clustering by columns, and ordering top-left to bottom-right. Images are anchored in the sequence based on proximity between image bounding boxes and text blocks.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF documents linked from CommonCrawl WAT files (February 2023 to April 2024 dumps). The raw data consists of PDF files downloaded from URLs extracted from CommonCrawl WAT dumps, containing text and images in arbitrary layouts.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data was collected from January 2024 to June 2024. The PDF source data comes from CommonCrawl WAT files from February 2023 to April 2024 dumps.
rai:dataLimitations: 1) PDF reading order extraction using PyMuPDF sometimes fails: incorrect reading across column boundaries and incorrect starting column. 2) PyMuPDF sometimes fails to detect images in PDFs. 3) The dataset is not self-contained and relies on downloading external image URLs; there are no guarantees these URLs will remain available over time (link rot). 4) The dataset may contain confidential content sourced from the public web. 5) Future work should explore more ways to improve safety of multimodal internet data. 6) The dataset should not be used to train models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or for military applications.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Paragraph and document text deduplication using a Bloom Filter (false positive rate 0.01) on 13-gram paragraphs; documents where more than 80% of paragraphs are duplicates are discarded. Image deduplication within each CommonCrawl snapshot based on SHA256 hashes, removing images appearing more than ten times within a snapshot. Repeated images within a single document are removed, keeping only the first occurrence.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: 1) PDFs larger than 50MB or over 50 pages are discarded. 2) Pages with no text are excluded. 3) Reading order extraction via bounding box clustering of text blocks by columns, ordered top-left to bottom-right. 4) Non-English documents removed using Fasttext language identification (confidence threshold 0.65). 5) Documents with URLs containing NSFW substrings removed. 6) Text quality filtering using RefinedWeb methods (removing documents with excessive duplicate n-grams or low quality per MassiveText rules). 7) Image filtering: images smaller than 150px or larger than 20,000px removed; aspect ratio threshold of 3 applied for PDFs. 8) NSFW image detection applied; documents with any NSFW image discarded. 9) PII removal: email addresses replaced with templates, IP addresses replaced with randomly generated non-functional IPs.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is distributed via HuggingFace as JSON shards. The authors will actively respond to issues and maintain the dataset. Updates will be communicated through the README in the HuggingFace interface. An erratum will be present on the README of the HuggingFace dataset page. Older versions can be found using the Git history of the dataset repository. A Google form will be provided for opting data out of MINT-1T. Contributions can be made through the Pull Request mechanism of the HuggingFace interface.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MINT-1T is intended to make research into large multimodal models more accessible by providing a large-scale open-source dataset. The authors took steps to remove personally identifiable information (masking emails and IP addresses) and NSFW content. However, the dataset may still contain offensive, insulting, or threatening content from the web. Using the dataset to train models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or for military applications is considered inappropriate. A Google form will be provided for individuals to request removal of their data.
rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training large multimodal models that process multiple interleaved images and text. Other potential uses include training models for generating interleaved image-text sequences and building multimodal document retrieval systems.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: 1) Fasttext language identification model (confidence threshold 0.65) for filtering non-English documents. 2) NSFW image detector (GantMan/nsfw_model) for removing pornographic and undesirable images. 3) GPT-4 used to classify LDA topic words into domains (Health & Medicine, Science, Business, Humanities, etc.) for diversity analysis. 4) GPT-2 tokenizer used to calculate number of text tokens for document composition analysis. 5) PyMuPDF for PDF parsing and reading order extraction.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain images of individuals and text about specific individuals from the public web. It may also contain sensitive data such as race/ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, financial or health data. Email addresses and IP addresses are masked (emails replaced with templates like "email@example.com", IPs replaced with randomly generated non-functional IPs). The dataset does not explicitly identify subpopulations but such information may be extractable.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: No human annotation was performed; data is automatically collected and filtered from CommonCrawl PDFs.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No crowdworkers or human annotators were involved; only the authors of the work were involved in data collection.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No human annotation was performed on this dataset.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform used; data collection was automated from CommonCrawl PDFs.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation protocol; data was automatically parsed and filtered.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The datasheet explicitly states 'None' for missing information from individual instances.
